intent.raw_query: Hawaii family beach vacation, $5000, 10 days, August from Seattle

selected_hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Maori. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional crafts, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing and an all-you-can-eat buffet. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the islands.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely day on one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand on Maui's west coast. Families can swim in calm turquoise waters, build sandcastles, rent boogie boards, and watch cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside restaurants and shave ice stands make it a perfect all-day outing.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, lomi salmon, poi, macaroni salad, and fresh poke bowls. Stop at legendary local institutions like Helena's Hawaiian Food and grab shave ice from Matsumoto's for dessert. A delicious and affordable way to connect the whole family with Hawaii's unique culinary heritage.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Hawaii
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration

Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Hawaii airport at 11:20 AM - collect luggage, pick up any pre-booked rental car or take TheBus (Oahu's public transit, ~$3/ride) to your accommodation. Check in or store luggage if room isn't ready yet.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Waikiki Beach (free entry) - just a short bus or walk from most Honolulu accommodations. Relax on the sand, swim in the calm waters, and let the kids splash around. Rent a bodyboard from a local vendor (~$10/hour) for extra fun.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Kalakaua Avenue, Waikiki's main strip. Watch the free hula and live music performances at Kuhio Beach Hula Mound (free, nightly shows around sunset). Grab dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick snack or coffee at the airport before or after landing - look for local plate lunch counters in the terminal.
meals.lunch: Rainbow Drive-In near Waikiki - iconic local plate lunch spot. Plate lunches from ~$10-13. Try the mixed plate with rice and macaroni salad.
meals.dinner: Marugame Udon in Waikiki - fresh udon noodles starting at ~$6, toppings and tempura add-ons are affordable. Great for families.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the late morning arrival. Pick up a reusable water bottle and sunscreen at a local ABC Store (chain convenience stores all over Waikiki) to save money throughout the trip. TheBus day pass is $7.50 and great value.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Diamond Head State Monument (Oahu) - a short hike to the crater summit with panoramic views of Honolulu and the coastline. Entry is $5/person. Start early (opens at 6 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. The 1.6-mile round trip is manageable for older kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve for snorkeling (one of Hawaii's best family snorkeling spots). Entry is $25/adult, children under 13 free. Snorkel rental on-site ~$15. Book online in advance as spots fill up fast. The bay is teeming with sea turtles and tropical fish.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Waikiki area. Walk through the International Marketplace (free to browse). Enjoy a relaxed evening near the beach.

meals.breakfast: Leonard's Bakery - famous for malasadas (Portuguese donuts) at ~$1.50 each. A beloved local institution and a must-try for families.
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a nearby grocery store (Times Supermarket or Foodland) to eat at Hanauma Bay - saves money and you can enjoy the beach setting.
meals.dinner: Ono Seafood - a tiny local gem serving poke bowls from ~$12-15. Fresh, authentic, and budget-friendly. Expect a short wait but worth it.

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay requires advance reservations online - book as soon as possible. Apply reef-safe sunscreen only (required by Hawaii law). August weather averages around 16-17°C overnight but daytime beach temps feel much warmer with sun.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the North Shore of Oahu - take TheBus Route 60 or drive (~1 hour from Waikiki). Visit Waimea Bay Beach Park (free) - a stunning beach with calm summer waters perfect for swimming and snorkeling in August.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the North Shore to Sunset Beach and Ehukai Beach Park (Banzai Pipeline). In August the waves are calm and safe for families. Walk the shoreline and look for sea turtles resting on the sand. Stop at Haleiwa town for shave ice.
day_by_day.evening: Drive or bus back toward Honolulu. Stop at a local grocery store to pick up supplies for a simple dinner back at the hotel to save money.

meals.breakfast: Boots & Kimo's Homestyle Kitchen in Kailua - famous for macadamia nut pancakes (~$14-16 per plate). A splurge-worthy family breakfast.
meals.lunch: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck in Haleiwa - legendary North Shore food truck. Shrimp plates ~$15. Cash only, so bring cash.
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner from Foodland or Times Supermarket - pick up poke, sushi rolls, fresh fruit, and local snacks. Budget ~$8-12 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The North Shore is about 35 miles from Waikiki. Renting a car for this day (~$40-60/day) gives the most flexibility. Alternatively, TheBus Route 60 runs the full route but takes about 2 hours each way. Bring cash for food trucks.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Pearl Harbor National Memorial (free entry to the grounds and museum exhibits). The USS Arizona Memorial boat tour is free but requires timed-entry passes - reserve online well in advance. An educational and moving experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ala Moana Beach Park (free) - a long, calm beach perfect for families with young children. The water is protected by a reef, making it very safe for swimming. Ala Moana Shopping Center is adjacent if you need anything.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Chinatown Honolulu - a vibrant neighborhood with affordable food stalls, local art galleries, and cultural shops. Safe and lively in the early evening.

meals.breakfast: Liliha Bakery - a Honolulu institution open since 1950. Try the coco puffs and breakfast plates for ~$8-12. Very family-friendly.
meals.lunch: Picnic at Ala Moana Beach Park - grab plate lunches from the nearby Ala Moana Food Court (budget ~$10-12 per person with lots of local options).
meals.dinner: Little Village Noodle House in Chinatown - generous portions of Chinese-Hawaiian fusion dishes. Most entrees ~$12-16, great for sharing as a family.

day_by_day.notes: Pearl Harbor timed-entry passes for the Arizona Memorial are free but extremely limited - book months in advance at recreation.gov. The grounds, museum, and film are free without a boat tour reservation. Allow at least 3-4 hours for the full experience.

day_by_day.morning: Inter-island flight or ferry to the Big Island (Hawaii Island) - book budget flights on Hawaiian Airlines or Southwest (~$60-120 one way if booked early). Fly into Kona or Hilo airport. This is the day to travel to the Big Island for the volcano experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive on the Big Island and head toward Hawaii Volcanoes National Park (entry $35/vehicle, valid 7 days). Stop at the Kilauea Visitor Center to get oriented, watch the orientation film, and pick up a free junior ranger booklet for kids.
day_by_day.evening: Drive the Crater Rim Drive to see the Kilauea caldera glowing at dusk - one of the most spectacular free natural light shows on Earth. The glow is most visible after dark. Visit the Jaggar Museum overlook area for the best views.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast at the Honolulu airport before your flight - look for local options like Honolulu Cookie Company or a plate lunch counter.
meals.lunch: Cafe Ono at the Volcano House Hotel inside the national park - sandwiches and soups ~$12-15. Convenient and reasonably priced given the location.
meals.dinner: Thai Thai Restaurant in Volcano Village just outside the park - authentic Thai food with generous portions. Most dishes ~$13-17. Very popular with locals.

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights as early as possible for the best budget fares. Rent a car on the Big Island - public transit is very limited. The national park entry fee covers all 7 days, so keep your receipt. Bring layers - Volcano area sits at 4,000 feet elevation and can be cool and rainy (average 176mm rain this month).

day_by_day.morning: Full day at Hawaii Volcanoes National Park. Start with the Kilauea Iki Trail (4-mile loop, 2-3 hours) - hike across a solidified lava lake and through lush rainforest. This is a moderate hike suitable for older children and a truly unique geological experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive Chain of Craters Road (19 miles one way, free with park entry) down to the coast. See ancient lava flows that buried entire communities, sea arch formations, and petroglyphs at the Pu'u Loa Petroglyph Trail (easy 1.4-mile round trip). Watch for sea turtles at the coast.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kilauea caldera for sunset and evening glow viewing. The colors of the lava lake reflecting off volcanic gases at dusk are unforgettable. Check with rangers for current eruption activity updates.

meals.breakfast: Pick up groceries from KTA Super Stores in Hilo or Keaau the day before - make a simple hotel room breakfast with local fruits like papaya and banana (~$5-8 per person).
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch to eat at one of the park's scenic overlooks - sandwiches, local chips, and fresh fruit. Saves time and money inside the park.
meals.dinner: Kilauea General Store in Volcano Village - casual local diner with plate lunches, burgers, and local specials. Budget ~$10-14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Wear sturdy closed-toe shoes for lava field hiking - the terrain is extremely rough. Bring plenty of water (at least 2 liters per person) as there are limited water sources in the park. Check nps.gov/havo for current eruption status and any trail closures before heading out.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Punalu'u Black Sand Beach (about 45 minutes south of the park) - one of Hawaii's most famous black sand beaches formed by lava meeting the ocean. Hawaiian green sea turtles (honu) regularly rest on the beach. Free entry, no swimming recommended but great for photos and turtle watching.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Hapuna Beach State Recreation Area on the Kohala Coast (about 1.5 hours from Punalu'u) - consistently rated one of Hawaii's best beaches. White sand, calm summer waters, and excellent snorkeling. Free parking and entry. Snorkel gear rental available nearby.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Kawaihae Harbor area or drive into Waimea (Kamuela) town for dinner. Waimea is a charming upcountry town with local restaurants and a cooler climate.

meals.breakfast: Holuakoa Gardens & Cafe in Holualoa village - charming coffee farm cafe with local pastries and Kona coffee. Budget ~$8-12 per person.
meals.lunch: Picnic at Hapuna Beach - bring supplies from KTA Super Stores. Fresh poke from the deli counter, rice, and local snacks make a perfect beach lunch.
meals.dinner: Merriman's Market Cafe in Waimea - farm-to-table casual dining using local Big Island ingredients. Lunch/dinner plates ~$15-20. A slight splurge but excellent quality.

day_by_day.notes: Do NOT approach or touch the sea turtles at Punalu'u - it is illegal under federal law and carries heavy fines. Maintain at least 10 feet distance. Hapuna Beach has lifeguards on duty in summer. The drive between the volcano area and Kohala Coast is scenic but long - plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Kealakekua Bay State Historical Park - a marine sanctuary and the site where Captain Cook first landed in Hawaii. Take a kayak tour (~$40-50/person for guided tours, or rent kayaks for ~$25-35) across the bay to the Captain Cook Monument. The snorkeling here is among the best in all of Hawaii.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive through the Kona Coffee Belt - stop at a free coffee farm tour (Greenwell Farms or Kona Joe Coffee offer free tours). Sample world-famous Kona coffee and learn about the growing process. Browse the Kailua-Kona waterfront area and Ali'i Drive.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Kailua Pier in Kona - watch the manta ray boats depart and enjoy the harbor atmosphere. Browse the free Hulihee Palace grounds (exterior) and Mokuaikaua Church.

meals.breakfast: Island Lava Java in Kailua-Kona - popular breakfast spot with ocean views. Breakfast plates ~$12-15. Try the local eggs Benedict with kalua pork.
meals.lunch: Da Poke Shack in Kailua-Kona - award-winning poke bowls from ~$13-16. Fresh, local, and absolutely delicious. Small spot so expect a wait.
meals.dinner: Umekes Fish Market Bar & Grill - casual waterfront dining with fresh fish tacos, poke, and local plates. Most items ~$12-18. Great family atmosphere.

day_by_day.notes: Kealakekua Bay kayak tours must be booked in advance - spots fill up quickly in August. The bay is a protected marine sanctuary so only guided tours can land at the monument. Bring reef-safe sunscreen. Kona is sunnier and drier than the Hilo/Volcano side - expect warm, sunny weather.

day_by_day.morning: Fly back to Oahu (book early morning flight to maximize the day, ~$60-100). Upon arrival, head to Kailua Beach on the windward side of Oahu - consistently ranked among America's best beaches. Calm, turquoise waters and white sand. Free entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent kayaks or stand-up paddleboards at Kailua Beach Adventures (~$25-35/hour) and paddle out to the Mokulua Islands (twin offshore islands). The water is crystal clear and the scenery is stunning. A great family adventure.
day_by_day.evening: Drive the scenic Pali Highway back to Honolulu. Stop at the Nu'uanu Pali Lookout (free) for dramatic views of the windward coast and the Ko'olau Mountains. Arrive back in Waikiki for a final evening.

meals.breakfast: Airport breakfast before your flight - grab a quick local option or pack snacks from the hotel.
meals.lunch: Kalapawai Market in Kailua - beloved local deli and market with fresh sandwiches, salads, and local specialties. Budget ~$10-14 per person.
meals.dinner: Duke's Waikiki - a Waikiki institution with ocean views. Happy hour (3-6 PM) offers discounted appetizers and drinks. Dinner entrees ~$18-28. A slightly special final Oahu dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Book the inter-island return flight as early as possible. Kailua is about 30 minutes from Waikiki by car. Parking at Kailua Beach is free but limited - arrive early. The Pali Lookout can be very windy - hold onto hats and small children. This is a wonderful contrast to the volcanic Big Island experience.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Hawaii - take a leisurely walk along the Ala Wai Canal path (free) or do some last-minute souvenir shopping at the International Marketplace or Ala Moana Center. For budget souvenirs, ABC Stores have affordable options, or visit the Aloha Stadium Swap Meet (open Wed, Sat, Sun - $1 entry) for the best deals on local crafts and gifts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport for departure. Allow at least 2.5-3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. TheBus Route 20 goes directly to the airport from Waikiki (~$3).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Honolulu. Reflect on an incredible 10-day Hawaiian adventure filled with volcanic landscapes, stunning beaches, sea turtles, world-class snorkeling, and authentic local food.

meals.breakfast: One last shave ice from Matsumoto Shave Ice (if near North Shore) or Waiola Shave Ice in Honolulu - a perfect sweet Hawaiian farewell. Pair with a plate lunch for a full meal.
meals.lunch: Zippy's Restaurant - a beloved local Hawaii chain with affordable plate lunches, saimin (local noodle soup), and chili. Budget ~$8-12 per person. A true local experience.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal - grab a snack at the airport. Look for local options like Makai Market food court in the terminal.

day_by_day.notes: Budget summary tips: Use TheBus on Oahu ($7.50 day pass) to save on transportation. Pack snacks and picnic lunches frequently. Book inter-island flights and popular attractions (Hanauma Bay, Pearl Harbor) months in advance for best prices. Look for free activities - many of Hawaii's best experiences cost nothing. Total estimated daily budget per person (excluding flights and accommodation): $60-90/day covering food, local transport, and activities.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrives at 11:20 AM — no morning activities scheduled. Upon landing, collect luggage, pick up rental car or arrange shuttle transfer to accommodation area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park. Freshen up and take a leisurely stroll around the Buena Park/Anaheim area to get oriented. Visit a nearby grocery or convenience store to stock up on snacks and essentials for the trip.
day_by_day.evening: Easy, low-key first evening — explore the Buena Park dining strip along Beach Boulevard. Window-shop and relax after the flight. Early bedtime to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light meal at the airport before or after landing — try a local Hawaiian-style café in the terminal if available.
meals.lunch: Pick up a casual bite near the hotel — Raising Cane's or In-N-Out Burger on Beach Blvd for a quick, affordable post-travel meal (~$10–15/person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sizzler on Beach Blvd or nearby Denny's for a relaxed, family-friendly, budget-conscious meal (~$15–20/person).

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is intentionally light given the 11:20 AM arrival. Prioritize rest and settling in. Confirm any pre-booked Hawaii activity reservations and review the upcoming itinerary as a family.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Knott's Berry Farm (just 5 minutes from the hotel on Beach Blvd) — a classic Southern California theme park perfect for families. Arrive at opening (10 AM) to beat crowds. Enjoy rides like GhostRider and Snoopy-themed areas for younger kids.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Knott's Berry Farm through the afternoon. Try the iconic Boysenberry-themed food offerings throughout the park. Visit Camp Snoopy for family-friendly rides and photo opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the hotel to freshen up, then explore Downtown Disney or the Anaheim GardenWalk for evening entertainment and dining (10–15 min drive).

meals.breakfast: Hotel continental breakfast or grab pastries and coffee at a nearby Starbucks or Panera Bread before heading to the park.
meals.lunch: Lunch inside Knott's Berry Farm — try the famous Mrs. Knott's Chicken Dinner Restaurant for their signature fried chicken (~$20–25/person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bubba Gump Shrimp Co. at Anaheim GardenWalk for a fun, family-friendly seafood experience (~$20–30/person).

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Knott's Berry Farm tickets online in advance for discounts (typically $30–50/person vs. gate price). Check the park's website for any seasonal August events or shows.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Disneyland Park (15-minute drive from hotel). Arrive at rope drop (8–9 AM) to maximize time. Head straight to popular rides like Space Mountain, Pirates of the Caribbean, and Haunted Mansion before crowds build.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Disneyland — explore Fantasyland and Tomorrowland with the family. Catch a midday parade or character meet-and-greet. Use the Disneyland app to manage wait times and Lightning Lane selections.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the spectacular Disneyland fireworks show (seasonal, typically 9 PM in August). Enjoy the magical atmosphere of Main Street USA lit up at night before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel or grab a quick bite at a nearby McDonald's before park opening to save time.
meals.lunch: Lunch inside Disneyland at the Plaza Inn on Main Street USA — known for their fried chicken and character dining (~$20–25/person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Blue Bayou Restaurant inside Disneyland for a memorable, atmospheric dining experience alongside the Pirates of the Caribbean ride (~$35–45/person — a mid-range splurge worth it for families).

day_by_day.notes: Book Blue Bayou Restaurant reservations well in advance via the Disneyland app. Purchase park tickets online ahead of time. August is peak season — expect crowds. Arrive early and use the app strategically.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Disney California Adventure Park (adjacent to Disneyland). Prioritize Radiator Springs Racers in Cars Land and Guardians of the Galaxy — Mission: BREAKOUT! early in the morning before lines grow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Pixar Pier and enjoy family-friendly rides like the Incredicoaster and Toy Story Midway Mania. Catch the Pixar Play Parade in the afternoon for a colorful, entertaining show.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the World of Color nighttime water and light spectacular at Paradise Bay (check schedule for August show times). A stunning visual experience for the whole family.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel — take advantage of the continental breakfast to save money before a full park day.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Flo's V8 Café in Cars Land for a themed, fun dining experience with classic American comfort food (~$18–22/person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Carthay Circle Restaurant in California Adventure for a refined yet family-friendly atmosphere with California-inspired cuisine (~$30–40/person).

day_by_day.notes: A Park Hopper ticket allows access to both Disneyland and California Adventure on the same day — useful if you want to revisit Disneyland in the evening. Check the Disneyland app for World of Color viewing area reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Huntington Beach (approx. 30–35 minutes from hotel) — known as 'Surf City USA.' Arrive early to claim a good spot on the wide, sandy beach. Rent beach chairs and an umbrella from a local vendor. Enjoy the ocean, build sandcastles, and soak up the California sun.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Huntington Beach Pier — one of the longest piers on the West Coast at 1,850 feet. Browse the surf shops and boutiques along Pacific Coast Highway. Consider a beginner surf lesson for the family through a local surf school (~$60–80/person for a 1.5-hour group lesson).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through downtown Huntington Beach's Main Street for shopping and dining. Enjoy the laid-back beach town atmosphere as the sun sets over the Pacific.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Eggs N' Things or a local diner near the hotel before heading to the beach.
meals.lunch: Casual beachside lunch at Duke's Huntington Beach — a Hawaiian-themed restaurant right on the sand with great ocean views (~$20–28/person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Wahoo's Fish Taco on Main Street Huntington Beach — fresh, flavorful, and very family-friendly (~$12–18/person).

day_by_day.notes: Huntington Beach is a great preview of the beach lifestyle you'll experience in Hawaii. Parking near the pier can be busy — arrive before 10 AM or use the city parking structure on 5th Street. Bring sunscreen, water, and beach toys for the kids.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Aquarium of the Pacific in Long Beach (approx. 35–40 minutes from hotel). One of the largest aquariums in the US, it's perfect for families and features over 11,000 animals. Highlights include the Shark Lagoon, Tropical Pacific Gallery, and the new Tidepool exhibit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Queen Mary historic ship docked in Long Beach Harbor — a fascinating floating museum and National Historic Landmark. Walk the decks, explore the exhibits, and learn about its storied history. Kids love the interactive displays.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Long Beach's Pine Avenue dining and entertainment district. Enjoy the waterfront atmosphere of Shoreline Village with harbor views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel or grab coffee and pastries at a local café before the drive to Long Beach.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Aquarium of the Pacific's Café Scuba — convenient and reasonably priced for a museum café (~$15–20/person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Parker's Lighthouse in Long Beach — a beloved seafood restaurant with stunning harbor views and a family-friendly menu (~$25–35/person).

day_by_day.notes: Combo tickets for the Aquarium of the Pacific and Queen Mary are available and offer savings. The Aquarium costs approximately $30–35/adult and $20–25/child. Book online for discounts. This is a great educational day for kids before the Hawaii trip.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour — start the morning with a drive to a local Hawaiian restaurant in the greater Los Angeles area (several excellent options within 30–45 minutes). Visit L&L Hawaiian Barbecue or Ono Hawaiian BBQ for an authentic taste of Hawaii's iconic plate lunch culture featuring kalua pork, macaroni salad, and two scoops of rice.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the La Brea Tar Pits and Museum in Los Angeles (approx. 40 minutes from hotel) — a unique, family-friendly attraction where you can see real Ice Age fossils being excavated. Afterward, stroll through the adjacent Hancock Park.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to the Santa Monica Pier (approx. 45–50 minutes) for a classic Southern California evening experience. Enjoy the Pacific Park amusement rides, street performers, and the iconic sunset over the Pacific Ocean.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel to save appetite for the food tour.
meals.lunch: The Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour IS lunch — visit two or three Hawaiian spots to sample different dishes (~$15–20/person total). Try spam musubi, loco moco, and shave ice for dessert.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bubba Gump Shrimp Co. on the Santa Monica Pier for a fun, ocean-view dining experience (~$22–30/person).

day_by_day.notes: The Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour experience is adapted to the LA area since you're still in California. This serves as a wonderful cultural and culinary preview of what to expect in Hawaii. Saturday traffic to Santa Monica can be heavy — plan accordingly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Universal Studios Hollywood (approx. 35–40 minutes from hotel). Arrive at opening to experience The Wizarding World of Harry Potter and Super Nintendo World before peak crowds. These are the most popular areas and worth prioritizing.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through Universal Studios — enjoy the Studio Tour tram ride, Jurassic World ride, and Despicable Me Minion Mayhem. Check the show schedule for WaterWorld and Special Effects Show performances.
day_by_day.evening: CityWalk at Universal Studios offers great evening dining and entertainment options. Browse the shops, enjoy street performers, and wind down after a full day at the park.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before heading to Universal Studios.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Three Broomsticks in The Wizarding World of Harry Potter — try the Great Feast or Butterbeer for a magical experience (~$20–25/person).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Voodoo Doughnut or Antojitos Authentic Mexican Food at CityWalk for a fun, casual end to the day (~$15–20/person).

day_by_day.notes: Purchase Universal Studios tickets online in advance for savings. Consider the Express Pass if budget allows — it significantly reduces wait times. August is peak season so the park will be busy. Arrive 30 minutes before official opening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County (approx. 35 minutes from hotel) — home to one of the world's most extensive collections of dinosaur fossils. The Dinosaur Hall and the Gem and Mineral Hall are highlights for families. The museum opens at 9:30 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Griffith Park and the Griffith Observatory (approx. 40 minutes from hotel). Enjoy panoramic views of Los Angeles and the Hollywood Sign. The Observatory is free to enter and offers fascinating astronomy exhibits. Hike the easy trail to the observatory from the parking area.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed final evening near the hotel — visit the Buena Park Downtown shopping center or stroll through the neighborhood. Pack bags and prepare for checkout the following day.

meals.breakfast: Sit-down breakfast at IHOP or Denny's near the hotel for a hearty family meal (~$12–18/person).
meals.lunch: Lunch at the museum café at the Natural History Museum or pack a picnic to enjoy at Griffith Park (~$10–15/person).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at BJ's Restaurant & Brewhouse in Buena Park — a family-friendly chain with a wide menu and great deep-dish pizzas (~$18–25/person).

day_by_day.notes: The Natural History Museum admission is approximately $15–18/adult and $7–10/child. Griffith Observatory is free but parking can be limited — consider the DASH Observatory bus from Los Feliz. This is a great low-key day before checkout.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park. Depending on departure flight time, enjoy a final California breakfast at a local favorite. If time permits, make a quick stop at Knott's Marketplace (the outdoor shopping area adjacent to Knott's Berry Farm — free to enter) to pick up souvenirs and famous Knott's boysenberry jam.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) or John Wayne Airport (SNA) depending on your departure flight — allow 45–60 minutes for the drive plus extra time for traffic. Return rental car if applicable. Complete check-in and security procedures.
day_by_day.evening: Depart from Southern California. Reflect on a wonderful 10-day balanced family trip combining theme parks, beaches, cultural experiences, and a taste of Hawaiian cuisine and culture in preparation for a future Hawaii visit.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Cracker Barrel on Beach Blvd or a local favorite diner near the hotel (~$12–16/person).
meals.lunch: Grab lunch at the airport — allow extra time to find a good option beyond fast food. Most major airports have sit-down restaurants airside (~$15–20/person).
meals.dinner: Dinner on the plane or upon arrival at your home destination.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before your flight for airport check-in, security, and boarding — especially with a family. Double-check all luggage weight limits. Keep all travel documents, passports, and boarding passes easily accessible. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Hawaii Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim

experiences.name: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay
experiences.description: Explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries with crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish and sea turtles. Perfect for families with kids of all ages, the bay offers calm, shallow waters ideal for beginner snorkelers. Equipment rentals are available on-site and an educational center teaches visitors about the reef ecosystem before entering the water.

experiences.name: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit
experiences.description: Spend a full day immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures including Hawaiian, Samoan, Tongan, Fijian, Tahitian, and Maori. Enjoy live demonstrations, canoe rides, traditional crafts, and an incredible evening luau with fire knife dancing and an all-you-can-eat buffet. One of the most educational and entertaining family experiences on the islands.

experiences.name: Kaanapali Beach Family Day
experiences.description: Spend a leisurely day on one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand on Maui's west coast. Families can swim in calm turquoise waters, build sandcastles, rent boogie boards, and watch cliff divers leap from Black Rock (Puu Kekaa) at sunset. Beachside restaurants and shave ice stands make it a perfect all-day outing.

experiences.name: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration
experiences.description: Witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes on the Big Island. Walk through lava tubes, hike across hardened lava fields, and peer into the glowing Kilauea caldera at dusk for a truly unforgettable family experience. The park's visitor center offers ranger-led programs designed specifically for children, making it both thrilling and educational.
experiences.location: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, Big Island

experiences.name: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour
experiences.description: Dive into authentic Hawaiian comfort food by visiting iconic local spots serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, lomi salmon, poi, macaroni salad, and fresh poke bowls. Stop at legendary local institutions like Helena's Hawaiian Food and grab shave ice from Matsumoto's for dessert. A delicious and affordable way to connect the whole family with Hawaii's unique culinary heritage.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at 11:20 AM — Flight Alaska lands. Clear immigration, collect luggage, and arrange private luxury transfer to hotel. Check in early if possible at SureStay Hotel by Best Western Buena Park Anaheim and freshen up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Settle into the hotel and take a leisurely stroll around the Buena Park area. Visit the nearby Knott's Berry Farm or relax at the hotel pool to recover from travel. Light exploration of the local neighborhood to get oriented.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at a nearby upscale restaurant. Enjoy a relaxed first evening, review the Hawaii itinerary ahead, and get a good night's rest before the main journey begins.

meals.breakfast: In-flight meal or grab a premium snack at the airport upon arrival
meals.lunch: The Catch Restaurant & Bar near Buena Park — fresh seafood in a relaxed upscale setting
meals.dinner: Mastro's Ocean Club at nearby South Coast Plaza — world-class steakhouse and seafood with an elegant atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Note: The hotel is located in Buena Park, California — this is the pre-Hawaii staging night. Confirm onward flights to Hawaii for the next morning. Pack light beach and family-friendly gear. Weather in Hawaii averages 16.8°C highs with some rain, so pack a light rain jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Early checkout and private luxury transfer to LAX or John Wayne Airport. Board morning flight to Honolulu, Oahu. Upon arrival in Hawaii, check in to a luxury Waikiki beachfront resort (upgrade recommended: The Royal Hawaiian or Halekulani Hotel). Unpack and change into beach attire.
day_by_day.afternoon: First taste of Hawaii — head directly to Waikiki Beach for a relaxed afternoon. Enjoy the warm Pacific waters, rent premium beach chairs and umbrellas, and let the family soak in the iconic views of Diamond Head. Optional: book a private outrigger canoe experience along the shore.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the beachfront bar of your resort, followed by a premium Hawaiian dinner experience. Watch the famous Waikiki sunset paint the sky in gold and pink.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the airport lounge before departure
meals.lunch: Duke's Waikiki — legendary oceanfront restaurant with fresh Hawaiian fish tacos and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: La Mer at Halekulani Hotel — Honolulu's most celebrated fine dining restaurant with French-Hawaiian cuisine and ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Arrange airport-to-resort private transfer in advance. Confirm luxury resort reservation. Apply reef-safe sunscreen — required at Hanauma Bay and recommended island-wide. Keep rain jackets accessible as August can bring brief afternoon showers.

day_by_day.morning: Snorkeling at Hanauma Bay — depart early (7:00 AM recommended) to secure entry as daily visitor numbers are capped. Watch the mandatory marine education video, then explore one of Hawaii's most pristine marine sanctuaries. Crystal-clear waters teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant coral make this a world-class family snorkeling experience. Rent premium snorkel gear on-site or bring your own.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Waikiki and enjoy a leisurely afternoon at the resort pool or beach. Optional: book a private surf lesson for the family on the gentle Waikiki waves — instructors are available for all ages and skill levels. Explore the upscale shops along Kalakaua Avenue.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a premium luau experience — book the Paradise Cove Luau or a private resort luau for an authentic Hawaiian cultural evening with fire dancers, hula performances, and a traditional imu (underground oven) feast.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departing for Hanauma Bay — order room service or visit the resort restaurant
meals.lunch: Koko Head Café near Hanauma Bay — beloved local brunch spot with creative Hawaiian-inspired dishes
meals.dinner: Paradise Cove Luau inclusive feast, or Nobu Honolulu for a world-renowned Japanese-Hawaiian fusion dinner

day_by_day.notes: Hanauma Bay reservations must be made online in advance — slots fill up weeks ahead. Arrive early to avoid crowds. The bay is closed on Tuesdays. Bring water shoes for the rocky entry points. Children of all ages love the shallow inner reef area.

day_by_day.morning: Polynesian Cultural Center Visit — drive approximately 35 miles north to Laie on the windward coast. Spend the full morning immersing the family in the rich traditions of six Polynesian cultures: Hawaii, Samoa, Tonga, Fiji, Tahiti, and Aotearoa (New Zealand). Participate in hands-on cultural demonstrations including fire-making, coconut husking, and traditional weaving.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Polynesian Cultural Center — enjoy the canoe pageant on the lagoon, watch cultural performances, and explore each village at your own pace. Upgrade to the Ali'i (VIP) package for reserved seating, behind-the-scenes access, and premium dining.
day_by_day.evening: Stay for the spectacular 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show — a world-class theatrical production featuring over 100 performers, stunning costumes, and the story of a Polynesian family across generations. One of Hawaii's most celebrated entertainment experiences.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort before departing — try the resort's signature Hawaiian breakfast with fresh tropical fruits and macadamia nut pancakes
meals.lunch: Gateway Restaurant at the Polynesian Cultural Center — included with Ali'i package, featuring Hawaiian and Polynesian-inspired buffet
meals.dinner: Ali'i Luau at the Polynesian Cultural Center — premium all-inclusive feast with imu-roasted kalua pig, poi, lomi salmon, and haupia dessert

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ali'i VIP package well in advance — it includes priority seating for the evening show, a premium buffet, and exclusive cultural experiences. The drive along the windward coast is scenic; consider stopping at the Nuuanu Pali Lookout on the way for panoramic views. Allow a full day — the center is best enjoyed without rushing.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Hawaiian Plate Lunch Food Tour — embark on a guided premium food tour of Honolulu's most iconic local spots. Visit legendary establishments serving plate lunches featuring kalua pork, loco moco, garlic shrimp, macaroni salad, and two scoops of rice. Learn about the history of Hawaii's multicultural food traditions from Japanese, Filipino, Korean, and native Hawaiian influences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Chinatown Honolulu and the historic downtown district. Visit the Iolani Palace — the only royal palace on American soil — for a guided tour of Hawaii's royal history. Browse the Honolulu Museum of Art for world-class Pacific and Asian art collections. Stop at a shave ice stand for the quintessential Hawaiian treat.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cruise along the Waikiki coastline — book a private luxury catamaran sunset sail with champagne, appetizers, and stunning views of Diamond Head and the Honolulu skyline as the sun dips below the horizon.

meals.breakfast: Café Kaila in Market City — beloved local breakfast spot with creative eggs Benedict and fresh-baked pastries
meals.lunch: Plate lunch food tour covers multiple tastings across several iconic local spots including Helena's Hawaiian Food (James Beard Award winner)
meals.dinner: Senia Restaurant — Honolulu's acclaimed farm-to-table fine dining experience with innovative Hawaiian cuisine by James Beard-nominated chefs

day_by_day.notes: Book the sunset catamaran cruise in advance through your resort concierge — private charters offer the most premium experience. The food tour is best done on an empty stomach. Iolani Palace requires advance reservations for guided tours. Chinatown is vibrant and family-friendly during daytime hours.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Honolulu (HNL) to Kahului, Maui (OGG) — short inter-island flight (approximately 30 minutes). Arrange private luxury transfer to a premium Kaanapali resort (recommended: Hyatt Regency Maui or Westin Maui Resort & Spa). Check in and head straight to the legendary Kaanapali Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Kaanapali Beach Family Day — spend a leisurely afternoon on one of America's most celebrated beaches stretching nearly three miles of golden sand. Rent premium beach equipment, try stand-up paddleboarding, or take a family snorkel along the Black Rock (Pu'u Keka'a) promontory where sea turtles and tropical fish are abundant. Watch cliff divers perform the traditional Hawaiian torch-lighting and cliff-diving ceremony.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the famous Kaanapali sunset — one of Maui's most spectacular. Attend the nightly torch-lighting ceremony at Black Rock, then dine at a beachfront restaurant with front-row sunset views.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Honolulu resort before the flight, or grab pastries and coffee at the airport
meals.lunch: Leilani's on the Beach at Whalers Village — open-air beachfront dining with fresh fish, burgers, and tropical cocktails right on Kaanapali Beach
meals.dinner: Japengo at Hyatt Regency Maui — award-winning Pacific Rim cuisine with sushi, fresh local fish, and stunning ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Book inter-island flights in advance — Hawaiian Airlines and Mokulele Airlines offer frequent service. Kaanapali Beach is consistently ranked among the top beaches in the USA. The Black Rock snorkel area is excellent for families — calm, clear water with abundant marine life. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Road to Hana — embark on one of the world's most scenic drives along Maui's northeastern coastline. Hire a private driver-guide for a premium, stress-free experience. Stop at Twin Falls for a refreshing swim, explore the lush Waikamoi Nature Trail, and marvel at the dramatic Ho'okipa Beach overlook where sea turtles bask on the shore.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Road to Hana journey — visit the stunning black sand beach at Waianapanapa State Park (advance reservations required), explore the sacred Oheo Gulch (Seven Sacred Pools) in Haleakala National Park, and discover hidden waterfalls along the route. The lush rainforest scenery is magical even with light rain.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kaanapali resort via the scenic route or the faster inland road. Enjoy a relaxing evening at the resort spa — book premium couples or family spa treatments to soothe tired muscles after the day's adventure.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departing — fuel up for the long day ahead
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hana Ranch Restaurant in the town of Hana — fresh local ingredients in a charming ranch setting, or pack a premium picnic prepared by your resort
meals.dinner: Merriman's Maui in Kapalua — farm-to-table Hawaiian Regional Cuisine pioneer with panoramic ocean views and locally sourced ingredients

day_by_day.notes: The Road to Hana is approximately 65 miles with over 600 curves and 59 bridges — a private driver is strongly recommended for families. Waianapanapa State Park requires advance online reservations. Start early (7:00 AM) to beat crowds and maximize daylight. Bring motion sickness remedies for children if needed. Light rain along the route is common and adds to the lush beauty.

day_by_day.morning: Haleakala Sunrise Experience — wake at 2:30 AM for a private guided summit tour to witness the legendary sunrise above the clouds at Haleakala Crater (10,023 feet elevation). This sacred Hawaiian experience is breathtaking and unforgettable. Bring warm layers — summit temperatures can drop to near freezing. Advance National Park reservations are mandatory for sunrise entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend from Haleakala and return to the resort for a well-deserved rest. Enjoy a late brunch, then spend the afternoon at the resort pool or on Kaanapali Beach. Optional: book a private whale watching cruise (seasonal) or a family dolphin snorkel tour in the calm waters off West Maui.
day_by_day.evening: Premium luau experience on Maui — attend the Old Lahaina Luau (one of Hawaii's most authentic and acclaimed) or the Drums of the Pacific Luau at the Hyatt Regency for a spectacular evening of Hawaiian culture, music, and cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Pack premium snacks and hot coffee in a thermos for the Haleakala summit — no food available at the summit before sunrise
meals.lunch: Late brunch at Kimo's Restaurant in Lahaina — beloved local institution with fresh fish, macadamia nut pancakes, and ocean views
meals.dinner: Old Lahaina Luau — all-inclusive premium feast with traditional Hawaiian foods, open bar, and world-class cultural performances

day_by_day.notes: Haleakala sunrise reservations must be booked online at recreation.gov — they sell out weeks in advance. The summit is extremely cold before sunrise; bring heavy jackets, gloves, and warm layers for the entire family. The experience is considered one of the most spiritual and awe-inspiring in all of Hawaii. Children must be old enough to handle the early wake-up and cold temperatures.

day_by_day.morning: Fly from Kahului, Maui (OGG) to Kona, Big Island (KOA) — short inter-island flight. Arrange private transfer to a luxury resort on the Kohala Coast (recommended: Four Seasons Resort Hualalai or Mauna Kea Beach Hotel). Check in and enjoy the resort's world-class amenities including private beach access and multiple pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park Exploration — drive approximately 90 minutes to Hawaii Volcanoes National Park to witness the raw power of nature at one of the world's most active volcanic landscapes. Walk the Kilauea Iki Trail through a solidified lava lake, explore the Thurston Lava Tube, and visit the Jaggar Museum overlook for dramatic views of the active Halemaumau Crater. Check for current lava flow activity with park rangers.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Kohala Coast resort. If lava is flowing into the ocean (activity dependent), arrange a premium evening lava boat tour for a once-in-a-lifetime experience of molten lava meeting the sea. Otherwise, enjoy a spectacular sunset dinner at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Maui resort or airport lounge before the flight
meals.lunch: Café Ono at the Volcano Art Center near the national park — fresh local sandwiches and soups in a charming gallery setting
meals.dinner: Beach Tree Restaurant at Four Seasons Hualalai — elegant open-air dining with fresh local fish, wood-fired pizzas, and stunning Pacific Ocean views

day_by_day.notes: Hawaii Volcanoes National Park is open 24 hours — evening visits offer dramatic glowing crater views. Check the USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory website for current eruption activity before visiting. The drive from Kohala Coast to the park is scenic but long — consider hiring a private guide. Lava boat tours must be booked in advance and are weather/activity dependent.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on the Big Island — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at the resort and take one last swim at the beautiful Kohala Coast beach. Optional: book an early morning manta ray snorkel tour off the Kona coast — a magical experience swimming alongside gentle giant manta rays in the clear Pacific waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the historic Puuhonua o Honaunau National Historical Park (Place of Refuge) — a sacred and beautifully preserved ancient Hawaiian sanctuary. Explore the royal fishponds, carved ki'i akua (wooden idols), and learn about traditional Hawaiian culture and the kapu system. Stop at a local Kona coffee farm for a premium tasting tour of the world-famous Kona coffee.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the resort's signature restaurant. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day Hawaiian journey with the family. Pack and prepare for the return flight. Arrange private luxury transfer to Kona Airport (KOA) for the flight back to the mainland.

meals.breakfast: Grand breakfast at the Four Seasons or Mauna Kea resort — indulge in the full luxury spread with fresh tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, and Kona coffee
meals.lunch: Manago Hotel Restaurant in Captain Cook — a Big Island institution since 1917, famous for their pork chops and local comfort food
meals.dinner: CanoeHouse at Mauna Lani Resort — one of Hawaii's most iconic fine dining experiences with Pacific Rim cuisine, open-air oceanfront setting, and a legendary wine list

day_by_day.notes: Manta ray snorkel tours depart from Keauhou Bay — book through Manta Ray Advocates for an educational and responsible experience. Kona coffee farm tours are available at Greenwell Farms and Mountain Thunder — both offer premium tastings. Confirm return flight details and arrange airport transfer the night before. Allow extra time at Kona Airport as it can be busy. Mahalo for an unforgettable Hawaiian adventure!
